newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more weakness seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly lower after remaining within ranges established early on Tuesday as a gloomy mood continued to hang over the market after the previous day's sharp drop.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 35 points to close at 17,395 after hitting a low of 17,250.
"There was no news. It was mainly technical trading but people are worried about the outlook for the Japanese economy," said a trader with a local futures house.

He said the March Nikkei could break below the 17,000 support level and head for 16,500-16,600 in the absence of any official measures to shore up the stock market or speed up Japan's financial de-regulation.

Dealers said participants were anxious about the financial health of Japanese institutions after Monday's news that Kyotaru Co Ltd, a restaurant chain operator whose shares are listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's first section, had filed for protection from its creditors.
"People feel there's going to be more bad news coming. It might be some time before we see the Nikkei moving higher," said a trader with another local institution.
He said the March Nikkei needed to close above the 17,700 resistance level to stabilise its immediate downtrend, but added that this looked like a stubborn hurdle.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 311.3 against its opening 310.0 on turnover of 424 lots.
